steps.content:
7:00 p.m., January 21, N.F. 113
My Best Cool Car temporary filming spot

steps.speaker: Lynn
steps.content: Um... um... For the sake of the movie, OwO is focused on the script right now... I-I'll take over... today's vlog...
She sneaks a nervous glance at the people behind the camera.

steps.speaker: Love
steps.content: Ugh, this is too hard on her! I'll do it...

steps.speaker: Daisy
steps.content: You come back here! Don't be an obnoxious attention-seeker like you were at the radio station.

steps.speaker: Lynn
steps.content: Ahhh... I'm sorry for being an attention-seeker... I shouldn't be stealing the spotlight... Well, th-that's all for today! Hope everything goes well with OwO's script. See you guys next time!
Lynn runs away from the camera in panic. Good thing you stopped filming, or else this girl was so shy that she would have started crying.

steps.speaker: Lynn
steps.content: Sob... I'm sorry, I'm so useless... I had promised to help OwO out... Sob...

steps.speaker: Lynn
steps.content: How is OwO? Is she in a better mood now?
The usually noisy girl is sitting motionlessly in the distance, hugging her lion's head. For the first time, calm and quiet falls over My Best Cool Car Studios.

steps.speaker: Love
steps.content: Why is OwO sad? The new Stella movie is great! It's loads of fun! I really like the duck that pops out of nowhere.

steps.speaker: Love
steps.content: Should we go comfort her together? It's so quiet without her. Not used to it.

steps.speaker: Daisy
steps.content: We should, but not you, Love. You're not suited for this.

steps.speaker: Lynn
steps.content: ...Is it because of the pressure...? Writer's block is really hard to overcome... How can we help her...

steps.speaker: Option
options: Maybe that's not the only reason.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: I'll go check up on her.

steps.speaker: [Scene Change]
steps.content: *Omitted as instructed by the client*
You lighten your footsteps as you approach her. OwO isn't crying, nor does she look back. She just stares blankly at the skyscrapers on the other side of the Rust.
The blue critter is resting next to her. It looks over swiftly when it hears you approaching, but this time, it doesn't grow agitated. It just looks at OwO, then at you, then lies down whimpering.
What should you say to her? Maybe just... encourage her?

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: I know you're there.

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: The plot... I haven't figured it out yet. If I go on camera like this, I'd let everyone down...

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Everyone made it together. We're all friends from the same crew.
You walk over and sit down beside her.

steps.speaker: Option
options: We can also figure out the plot together.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Let's figure out how to add dazzling fantasy to Stella's story.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: What do you think, OwO? You want it to be more dazzling? More dreamy? Or perhaps more romantic?

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: ...I really don't know... what's missing, exactly...

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: Maybe it's what ${PlayerName} said... Realism?

steps.speaker: Option
options: Can dazzling fantasy and realism mix?

steps.content: She doesn't answer the question, but just shifts her gaze from the distance to the lion head in her hands.

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: Did you know? I'm the only one in DisCity who knows how to perform a lion dance. This lion head is also totally unique.

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: These are all special treasures from Goldionville.

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: Have you heard of Goldionville, ${PlayerName}?
You shake your head.

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: Hehe... Very few people know about it. But I learned of it when I was very little.

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: Goldionville is a tiny city-state far, far away from DisCity. The people there are completely different from the people here. They speak a different language, write a different script, wear different clothing, eat different food...

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: Oh, when they eat, they use two little bamboo sticks to pick up the food. It's really impressive. Even I had to practice a long time to get the hang of it!
She shows you a strange gesture.

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: They are completely different from the people of DisCity!

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: They're all so unique, just like OwO! Oh, but OwO is the best at lion dancing!

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: Goldionville is very far away. I haven't been there yet. I grew up here. DisCity is my home.

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: But I've heard of another term called "homeland." I think Goldionville is my homeland.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Why do you say that? Did someone tell you?

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: I found out myself.

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: Do you remember? I was born a much-loved child and raised by the whole Drifter Camp. All my neighbors, from the 1st floor to the 100th, loved and doted on me.

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: A few of them looked like me. We had the same hair, eyes and skin color.

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: They came only once in a blue moon. They were very busy and low-key people, who came and went cautiously and quietly. But each time, they'd make sure to come and see me, and give me lots of fun and yummy things.

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: I got my precious lion head from them, hehe!

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: The people in the Drifter Camp told me they were merchants from Goldionville, who trekked a long way here for DisCity's precious stones. They had to brave huge sandstorms and desert bandits along the way.

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: They never stayed for long, but always came to see me when they had time. They would smile at me and beat up my bullies. I found that each time they were about to leave, they would hide and secretly shed tears.

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: I found that... they were different from the other neighbors who loved me. Though I'm the most adorable cutie pie in the world, these merchants loved me more than anyone else.

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: So, gradually, I started praying for them to come. I really liked them, and wanted them to tell me stories about Goldionville.

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: They refused to tell me, and forbade me from learning the way they talk. They insisted that I use the language of DisCity. They only gave me this lion head because I threw a tantrum. Hmph! They didn't teach me how to use it. I taught myself!
The girl shakes the lion head grumpily, her expression darkening again.

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: They stopped coming for a long, long time... Some said the catastrophe became stronger, and now there's something called the Tide of Ashes. Merchant fleets from small places can't make it here anymore...

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: There, there. Since they can't come, it's up to you to call out to them. It's just like the movie for Stella, calling out to its faraway family. They will hear it.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Our goal is to win the DisCars. A DisCar-winning movie will be famous all over the world, and watched in every city-state, no matter how far away. Right?

Even if we don't win an award, as long as the movie gets made, there should be a way to get it out there. Your connections with the Outland Affairs Bureau, as well as the trade info you get, should be able to help.
Having been comforted by you, OwO breaks into a smile.

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: Stop! I'm the invincible Lion Dancing Queen, the star of tomorrow! Since when did a lowly clapper get to comfort me?

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: I'm super strong and confident! My lion dance became so awesome and unique precisely because the Goldionville folks didn't come often! Add in Stella's dazzling fantasy, and we'll win for sure!

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: As soon as we figure out the plotline, the DisCars are ours!

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: As long as we figure out how to send Stella home... As long as we figure out... Emmmm...
As she says this, she starts to rub her hair buns in worry again.

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: Sigh... It's weird no matter how I think about it! It just feels off that Stella's family would suddenly come back like that. So fake. Even I want to laugh at it...

steps.speaker: Option
options: Maybe you don't need that much realism for dazzling fantasy?

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: See, this is the problem... Sigh...
Um...
A huge electronic helmet suddenly looms behind you in silence. You notice it, startling each other.

steps.speaker: Lynn
steps.content: I-I didn't mean to scare you guys! I just wanted to help, so I searched up "movie" and "dazzling fantasy" online...

steps.speaker: Lynn
steps.content: I found an interview with a famous director... I really agree with the points she gave. Maybe it can also inspire you...
Lynn hands you the phone timidly. The title of the article is "Indelible Mark: Lost Interview with the Legendary Director Deren."

Deren:
Movies are often described as dream-makers that weave beautiful fantasies with lights and shadows. But I think it's a lot more complicated than dreams.

The audience always walks into the theater "sober." It's up to the filmmaker to challenge them to a game of truth and deception amidst the lights and shadows.

Research, props, backdrops, lighting, acting skills... These are only technical issues. Beyond these, one must convey emotions that cannot be described with words...

We go to great lengths to convince the audience to believe a lie, which takes just one little audio-visual slip up or plot hole to expose. It truly is difficult...

Hehe... but also very fascinating.

People know it's fake, yet choose to believe that it's true. That's the interesting part.
After reading the article, everyone falls silent.

steps.speaker: Lynn
steps.content: Oh... She's a famous Dillywood director who nabbed all the DisCars one year. She's quite the legend...

steps.speaker: Lynn
steps.content: So I think... to win a DisCar... or to solve OwO's problem, we can use her opinion as a reference?

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: Hmm... but I still have a question.

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: What does a director do again?

You almost choke. Seeing how confident she was ordering everyone around, you had assumed that she thought of herself as My Best Cool Car's director. Little did you know... Now, all you can do is try to explain as you scratch your head.

steps.speaker: Option
options: It's the soul of a film.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: In reference to what had been said, it's the person who directs the entire crew to realize the movie by using various technical tools, so that the audience may believe and enjoy it.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: It's kind of like what you're doing right now, OwO. But with more expertise and experience.
OwO goes deep into thought.

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: So... what I can't figure out now stems from not understanding "directing," and lacking "expertise" and "experience"?

steps.speaker: Lynn
steps.content: I... I didn't mean it that way. It's difficult, but with hard work, you should be able to do it...
Lynn tries frantically to comfort OwO, but OwO jumps up.

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: Oh, I get it now! Thanks, Lynn! I finally found the missing piece of the puzzle that stands between My Best Cool Car and the DisCars!

steps.speaker: OwO
steps.content: We need a director! Let's go to Dillywood to find Deren! We need her to join our crew!
